title: Lena and the Portrait
premise: Estate lawyer Sable Okafor is hired by a dying client, Marguerite Voss, who pays a fortune to prove that her ward, Lena, has not yet been murdered — a crime scheduled but not committed, with the statute of limitations ticking toward the date it becomes legally irrelevant. Following Voss's will, which bequeaths everything to a woman officially dead for six years, Sable uncovers a found family of forgers and archivists who faked Lena's death to protect her from the Voss fortune's true heirs. In the climax, Sable finds Lena alive in plain sight as the estate's own archivist, and together they expose the heir who ordered the killing; the will stands, Lena claims her name, and Sable — long invisible behind their profession — finally belongs to someone.
about_author: Zephyrine Almeida is the pen name of a former probate clerk who spent a decade reading other people's last words before writing her own first novel. She lives near a coastal archive town and collects wills she finds in secondhand books.

chapters.title: The Client Who Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Sable Okafor's POV. A frail Marguerite Voss retains Sable to prove a murder hasn't happened yet, paying triple and naming a dead woman, Lena, as sole heir. The retainer includes a sealed will dated next month. Sable, professionally detached and personally isolated, accepts out of curiosity more than belief. Emotional beat: unease disguised as professional interest.

chapters.title: A Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. At the county records office, Sable discovers Lena was declared dead six years ago — drowned, witnessed, closed case. Yet Voss's new will cites her as living 'as of this signing.' The old heirs, the Ashcombe cousins, have already sent lawyers sniffing around. Emotional beat: the thrill of an impossible document turning to dread.

chapters.title: Everyone Swears She's Dead
chapters.summary: Sable interviews the drowning's witnesses: a fisherman, a doctor, Voss's late housekeeper's daughter. Each account is polished, rehearsed, identical in its gaps. One witness, an old groundskeeper, trembles and says only: 'Ask whoever keeps her letters.' Emotional beat: the creeping sense that grief here is performance.

chapters.title: The House That Remembers
chapters.summary: Sable's POV at Voss Hall, ostensibly cataloguing assets. Rooms are preserved mid-life — a teacup still warm, a piano recently played. The staff move like people guarding something. Sable finds a hidden dumbwaiter shaft connecting the archive wing to the boathouse. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into surveillance; Sable realizes they're being watched too.

chapters.title: Letters from a Ghost
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins: brief interludes from 'L.,' writing unsent letters about watching strangers search for you while standing beside them. Sable decodes the groundskeeper's hint and finds correspondence hidden in the archive's false spines — letters proving Lena wrote them within the past year. Emotional beat: intimacy across distance; Sable speaks aloud to an empty room for the first time in years.

chapters.title: The Statute Burns Down
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The Ashcombes file to invalidate the will on death grounds, forcing a legal deadline: prove Lena alive before the limitation expires or the estate passes to them — and whoever wanted Lena dead walks free. Voss deteriorates rapidly; her nurse, Devi, slips Sable a key. Emotional beat: pressure mounting, allies appearing where Sable expected none.

chapters.title: What the Drowning Hid
chapters.summary: Devi's POV chapter. She reveals the conspiracy: Voss, the housekeeper, the fisherman staged Lena's death to shield her from cousin Edmund Ashcombe, who'd already tried once to kill her for the inheritance. Devi confesses her own role and her fear that Edmund has returned. Emotional beat: guilt, loyalty, and the cost of a lie kept lovingly for six years.

chapters.title: Edmund Comes Home
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Edmund arrives charming and litigious, probing Sable's findings over dinner. That night someone ransacks the archive — the letters are gone, and the groundskeeper is hospitalized after a 'fall.' Sable realizes the murder may no longer be pending; it may be rescheduled for tonight. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Witness in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Climax. Following the dumbwaiter shaft to the boathouse, Sable confronts Edmund attempting to finish what he started — and is saved when the archivist, quiet Miss Ellery, reveals herself as Lena, producing the recovered letters and a recording of Edmund's threats. Voss, wheeled down to witness, signs a codicil confirming identity before witnesses. Emotional beat: terror breaking open into recognition — Sable has known her all along.

chapters.title: Belonging, Notarized
chapters.summary: Resolution, Sable's POV. The court upholds the will; Edmund is charged; Voss dies peacefully knowing Lena is safe and named. Lena offers Sable not payment but a place — keeper of the archive, member of the strange family that faked a death to save a life. Sable, who built a career on witnessing endings, chooses instead to stay for beginnings. Emotional beat: quiet, earned belonging.
